---
title: "Biowulf Basics"
---

## Access and login

Request an NIH HPC account and group allocation before starting. Follow the official **[NIH HPC account instructions](https://hpc.nih.gov/docs/accounts.html)**. The account-request form is available only from the NIH network or VPN, and account approval requires your PI and the appropriate sponsoring information.

<div class="callout">
<strong>Individual accounts only.</strong> NIH HPC does not allow shared accounts or shared passwords. Keep your own account, SSH setup, and access approval current.
</div>

## File systems

Use the group-approved project and scratch locations. Keep raw files, databases, scripts, intermediate files, and final results in clearly named directories. Do not run intensive analyses on a login node.

## SLURM basics

SLURM schedules batch jobs on compute nodes. Every job script should record the resources requested, software version, input paths, output path, and analysis command.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=proteomics-test
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=32g
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x-%j.out

module load <approved-software-module>
<analysis-command>
```

<div class="callout">
Replace placeholders with group-approved modules and paths. Save the SLURM job ID and output log for every analysis.
</div>

## Before submitting a full analysis

1. Confirm the file paths and file names.
2. Test a small subset of raw files.
3. Inspect the log and output files.
4. Scale to the full dataset only after the test finishes correctly.
